First, calculate the inductance \( L \) of the solenoid:  

\[
L = \frac{\mu_0 N^2 A}{l}
\]
where  
\(\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \ \text{H/m}\)  
\(N = 1000\)  
\(l = 0.30 \ \text{m}\)  
Diameter \(= 0.03 \ \text{m} \Rightarrow A = \pi (0.015)^2 = \pi \times 2.25 \times 10^{-4} \ \text{m}^2\)  

\[
A \approx 7.0686 \times 10^{-4} \ \text{m}^2
\]
\[
L = \frac{(4\pi \times 10^{-7}) (1000^2) (7.0686 \times 10^{-4})}{0.30}
\]
\[
L \approx \frac{(4\pi \times 10^{-7})(10^6)(7.0686 \times 10^{-4})}{0.30}
\]
\[
4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 10^6 = 4\pi \times 10^{-1} \approx 1.256637
\]
Multiply by \(7.0686 \times 10^{-4}\):  
\[
1.256637 \times 7.0686 \times 10^{-4} \approx 8.882 \times 10^{-4}
\]
Divide by \(0.30\):  
\[
L \approx 2.9607 \times 10^{-3} \ \text{H}
\]

Energy stored:  
\[
W = \frac{1}{2} L I^2 = 0.5 \times 2.9607 \times 10^{-3} \times (10^2)
\]
\[
W \approx 0.5 \times 2.9607 \times 10^{-3} \times 100
\]
\[
W \approx 0.148035 \ \text{J} \approx 0.15 \ \text{J}
\]

That matches option (B).  

Final answer: (B)
